{{Location map|Japan Kyoto|lat_deg=34|lat_min=51|lat_sec=53.32|lon_deg=135|lon_min=46|lon_sec=44.19|label=Kutsukawa
Kofun Cluster|position=top|width=220|Red pog.svg|marksize=10|caption={{center|Location of the Kutsukawa Kofun Cluster}}}} '''Kutsukawa Kofun Cluster''' (久津川古墳群) is a group of [[kofun]] burial mounds located in {{ill|Joyo|ja|城陽市}}, Kyoto Prefecture, Japan. Part of the cluster is designated as a National Historic Site and represents one of the largest kofun groups in Kyoto Prefecture.[http://mj-ktmr2.digi2.jp/p26ky/pys26207kutugawa.htm Kofun of Joyo City] == Overview == The Kutsukawa Kofun Cluster is situated in the lowlands and hills surrounding the Otanigawa River, east of {{ill|Kintetsu|ja|近畿日本鉄道}}'s Kutsukawa Station. Narrowly defined, the cluster includes around ten kofun near {{ill|Kutsukawa Kurazuka Kofun|ja|久津川車塚古墳}}, but when including smaller kofun scattered throughout the nearby hills, the total number of burial mounds is estimated to be around 150.[http://www.kyoto-kankou.or.jp/info_search/?id=379&r=1441389345.907 Kyoto Tourism Guide: Joyo City Kutsukawa Kofun Cluster] Many kofun have been lost or obscured due to recent residential development.[https://bunka.nii.ac.jp/heritages/detail/138764 Cultural Heritage Online: Kutsukawa Kurazuka and Marutsuka Kofun] Previously, {{ill|Kutsukawa Kurazuka Kofun|ja|久津川車塚古墳}} and {{ill|Maruzuka Kofun (Jōyō City)|ja|丸塚古墳 (城陽市)}} were designated collectively as the National Historic Site "Kutsukawa Kurazuka and Marutsuka Kofun." In 2016, {{ill|Basho-zuka Kofun|ja|芭蕉塚古墳}} and {{ill|Kuse Elementary School Kofun|ja|久世小学校古墳}} were added to the designation, and the name was changed to "Kutsukawa Kofun Cluster."{{PDFlink|[https://www.bunka.go.jp/koho_hodo_oshirase/hodohappyo/pdf/2016061701_besshi03.pdf Regarding Designations of Historic Sites]}} (Agency for Cultural Affairs, June 17, 2016).Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology Notification No. 144, October 3, 2016. Separately, Shibagahara No. 12 Kofun has been designated as the National Historic Site "{{ill|Shibagahara Kofun|ja|芝ヶ原古墳}}" and is not part of the "Kutsukawa Kofun Cluster." == Major Kofun == * **{{ill|Kutsukawa Kurazuka Kofun|ja|久津川車塚古墳}}** - National Historic Site. The largest keyhole-shaped kofun in the cluster and one of the largest in the Yamashiro region. A {{ill|Nagashigata stone coffin|ja|長持形石棺}} made of Ryuzan stone was discovered here. * **{{ill|Maruzuka Kofun (Jōyō City)|ja|丸塚古墳 (城陽市)}}** - National Historic Site. A scallop-shaped kofun. * **{{ill|Aotsuka Kofun|ja|青塚古墳 (城陽市)}}** - Rectangular front and rear burial mound. * **{{ill|Akatsuka Kofun|ja|赤塚古墳 (城陽市)}}** - Round burial mound adjacent to {{ill|Hirakawa Temple Ruins|ja|平川廃寺跡}}. * **{{ill|Basho-zuka Kofun|ja|芭蕉塚古墳}}** - National Historic Site. Keyhole-shaped kofun. * **Kajizuka Kofun** - Square burial mound partially overlapping Kutsukawa Kurazuka Kofun. * **Shigetsuzuka Kofun** - Round burial mound previously located on the grounds of {{ill|Joyo Municipal Kutsukawa Elementary School|ja|城陽市立久津川小学校}} but now lost due to construction. * **Hakozuka Kofun** - Keyhole-shaped kofun. * **Yamamichi Kofun** - Square burial mound lost due to residential development. * **{{ill|Shibagahara Kofun Group|ja|芝ヶ原古墳群}}** - A group of 13 kofun. Shibagahara No. 12 Kofun is designated as the National Historic Site "{{ill|Shibagahara Kofun|ja|芝ヶ原古墳}}," while Shibagahara No. 9 Kofun, located in the courtyard of {{ill|Joyo Municipal Kuse Elementary School|ja|城陽市立久世小学校}}, is designated as "{{ill|Kuse Elementary School Kofun|ja|久世小学校古墳}}." * **{{ill|Nitsuka Kofun Group|ja|尼塚古墳群}}** - A group of seven kofun. Nos. 1–5 have been lost, while Nos. 6 and 7 are preserved. * **Kami-Otani Kofun Group** - A group of 20 kofun, with 11 preserved. * **Shimo-Otani Kofun Group** - A group of two kofun. No. 2 has been lost, while No. 1 is preserved. * **{{ill|Nishiyama Kofun Group|ja|西山古墳群 (城陽市)}}** - Formerly near the Shimo-Otani group but lost due to residential development. * **Otakeshi Kofun** - Square burial mound. * **{{ill|Anjiyama Kofun|ja|庵寺山古墳}}** - Round burial mound. == Other Sites == * **{{ill|Hirakawa Temple Ruins|ja|平川廃寺跡}}** - National Historic Site adjacent to Akatsuka Kofun. * **{{ill|Kuse Temple Ruins|ja|久世廃寺跡}}** - National Historic Site. * **{{ill|Seido Administrative Complex Ruins|ja|正道官衙遺跡}}** - National Historic Site. == Cultural Properties == === Important Cultural Properties (National Designation) === * **Mirrors excavated from Kutsukawa Kurazuka Kofun (7 pieces, archaeological artifacts)** - Stored at {{ill|Sen-oku Hakukokan Museum|ja|泉屋博古館}}. Designated on November 14, 1953.{{National Cultural Property Database|201|9721|Mirrors Excavated from Kutsukawa Kurazuka Kofun}} * **Artifacts excavated from Shibagahara Kofun in Kyoto Prefecture (archaeological artifacts)** - Stored at Joyo City Historical Museum. Designated on June 29, 1990.{{National Cultural Property Database|201|10078|Artifacts Excavated from Shibagahara Kofun}} * **Nagashigata Stone Coffin excavated from Kutsukawa Kurazuka Kofun (archaeological artifacts)** - Stored at Kyoto University. Designated on June 21, 1991.{{National Cultural Property Database|201|10083|Nagashigata Stone Coffin Excavated from Kutsukawa Kurazuka Kofun}} === National Historic Sites === * **Kutsukawa Kofun Cluster** ** Kutsukawa Kurazuka Kofun ** Marutsuka Kofun ** Basho-zuka Kofun ** Kuse Elementary School Kofun *: Designated on January 19, 1979, as "Kutsukawa Kurazuka and Marutsuka Kofun." *: Renamed "Kutsukawa Kofun Cluster" with the inclusion of Basho-zuka and Kuse Elementary School Kofun on October 3, 2016.{{National Cultural Property Database|401|1741|Kutsukawa Kofun Cluster}} * **Shibagahara Kofun** *: Designated on September 6, 1989. *: Boundary expanded on January 24, 2012.{{National Cultural Property Database|401|1750|Shibagahara Kofun}} === Joyo City Designated Cultural Properties === * **Artifacts Excavated from Shibagahara No. 11 Kofun (archaeological artifacts)** File:芝ヶ原11号墳出土 三角縁銘帯三神四獣鏡.JPG|Triangular-rimmed mirror excavated from Shibagahara No. 11 Kofun
{{small|Exhibited at the Joyo City Historical Museum (Gorikan).}} == Access == * Approximately 10–45 minutes on foot from {{ill|Kintetsu|ja|近畿日本鉄道}} Kutsukawa Station. * Approximately 10–45 minutes on Kofun Cluster|position=top|width=220|Red pog.svg|marksize=10|caption={{center|Location of the Kutsukawa Kofun Cluster}}}} '''Kutsukawa Kofun Cluster''' (久津川古墳群) is a group of [[kofun]] burial mounds located in {{ill|Joyo|ja|城陽市}}, Kyoto Prefecture, Japan. Part of the cluster is designated as a National Historic Site and represents one of the largest kofun groups in Kyoto Prefecture.[http://mj-ktmr2.digi2.jp/p26ky/pys26207kutugawa.htm Kofun of Joyo City] == Overview == The Kutsukawa Kofun Cluster is situated in the lowlands and hills surrounding the Otanigawa River, east of {{ill|Kintetsu|ja|近畿日本鉄道}}'s Kutsukawa Station. Narrowly defined, the cluster includes around ten kofun near {{ill|Kutsukawa Kurazuka Kofun|ja|久津川車塚古墳}}, but when including smaller kofun scattered throughout the nearby hills, the total number of burial mounds is estimated to be around 150.[http://www.kyoto-kankou.or.jp/info_search/?id=379&r=1441389345.907 Kyoto Tourism Guide: Joyo City Kutsukawa Kofun Cluster] Many kofun have been lost or obscured due to recent residential development.[https://bunka.nii.ac.jp/heritages/detail/138764 Cultural Heritage Online: Kutsukawa Kurazuka and Marutsuka Kofun] Previously, {{ill|Kutsukawa Kurazuka Kofun|ja|久津川車塚古墳}} and {{ill|Maruzuka Kofun (Jōyō City)|ja|丸塚古墳 (城陽市)}} were designated collectively as the National Historic Site "Kutsukawa Kurazuka and Marutsuka Kofun." In 2016, {{ill|Basho-zuka Kofun|ja|芭蕉塚古墳}} and {{ill|Kuse Elementary School Kofun|ja|久世小学校古墳}} were added to the designation, and the name was changed to "Kutsukawa Kofun Cluster."{{PDFlink|[https://www.bunka.go.jp/koho_hodo_oshirase/hodohappyo/pdf/2016061701_besshi03.pdf Regarding Designations of Historic Sites]}} (Agency for Cultural Affairs, June 17, 2016).Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology Notification No. 144, October 3, 2016. Separately, Shibagahara No. 12 Kofun has been designated as the National Historic Site "{{ill|Shibagahara Kofun|ja|芝ヶ原古墳}}" and is not part of the "Kutsukawa Kofun Cluster." == Major Kofun == * **{{ill|Kutsukawa Kurazuka Kofun|ja|久津川車塚古墳}}** - National Historic Site. The largest keyhole-shaped kofun in the cluster and one of the largest in the Yamashiro region. A {{ill|Nagashigata stone coffin|ja|長持形石棺}} made of Ryuzan stone was discovered here. * **{{ill|Maruzuka Kofun (Jōyō City)|ja|丸塚古墳 (城陽市)}}** - National Historic Site. A scallop-shaped kofun. * **{{ill|Aotsuka Kofun|ja|青塚古墳 (城陽市)}}** - Rectangular front and rear burial mound. * **{{ill|Akatsuka Kofun|ja|赤塚古墳 (城陽市)}}** - Round burial mound adjacent to {{ill|Hirakawa Temple Ruins|ja|平川廃寺跡}}. * **{{ill|Basho-zuka Kofun|ja|芭蕉塚古墳}}** - National Historic Site. Keyhole-shaped kofun. * **Kajizuka Kofun** - Square burial mound partially overlapping Kutsukawa Kurazuka Kofun. * **Shigetsuzuka Kofun** - Round burial mound previously located on the grounds of {{ill|Joyo Municipal Kutsukawa Elementary School|ja|城陽市立久津川小学校}} but now lost due to construction. * **Hakozuka Kofun** - Keyhole-shaped kofun. * **Yamamichi Kofun** - Square burial mound lost due to residential development. * **{{ill|Shibagahara Kofun Group|ja|芝ヶ原古墳群}}** - A group of 13 kofun. Shibagahara No. 12 Kofun is designated as the National Historic Site "{{ill|Shibagahara Kofun|ja|芝ヶ原古墳}}," while Shibagahara No. 9 Kofun, located in the courtyard of {{ill|Joyo Municipal Kuse Elementary School|ja|城陽市立久世小学校}}, is designated as "{{ill|Kuse Elementary School Kofun|ja|久世小学校古墳}}." * **{{ill|Nitsuka Kofun Group|ja|尼塚古墳群}}** - A group of seven kofun. Nos. 1–5 have been lost, while Nos. 6 and 7 are preserved. * **Kami-Otani Kofun Group** - A group of 20 kofun, with 11 preserved. * **Shimo-Otani Kofun Group** - A group of two kofun. No. 2 has been lost, while No. 1 is preserved. * **{{ill|Nishiyama Kofun Group|ja|西山古墳群 (城陽市)}}** - Formerly near the Shimo-Otani group but lost due to residential development. * **Otakeshi Kofun** - Square burial mound. * **{{ill|Anjiyama Kofun|ja|庵寺山古墳}}** - Round burial mound. == Other Sites == * **{{ill|Hirakawa Temple Ruins|ja|平川廃寺跡}}** - National Historic Site adjacent to Akatsuka Kofun. * **{{ill|Kuse Temple Ruins|ja|久世廃寺跡}}** - National Historic Site. * **{{ill|Seido Administrative Complex Ruins|ja|正道官衙遺跡}}** - National Historic Site. == Cultural Properties == === Important Cultural Properties (National Designation) === * **Mirrors excavated from Kutsukawa Kurazuka Kofun (7 pieces, archaeological artifacts)** - Stored at {{ill|Sen-oku Hakukokan Museum|ja|泉屋博古館}}. Part of the cluster is designated as a National Historic Site and represents one of the largest kofun groups in Kyoto Prefecture.[http://mj-ktmr2.digi2.jp/p26ky/pys26207kutugawa.htm Kofun of Joyo City] == Overview == The Kutsukawa Kofun Cluster is situated in the lowlands and hills surrounding the Otanigawa River, east of {{ill|Kintetsu|ja|近畿日本鉄道}}'s Kutsukawa Station. Narrowly defined, the cluster includes around ten kofun near {{ill|Kutsukawa Kurazuka Kofun|ja|久津川車塚古墳}}, but when including smaller kofun scattered throughout the nearby hills, the total number of burial mounds is estimated to be around 150.[http://www.kyoto-kankou.or.jp/info_search/?id=379&r=1441389345.907 Kyoto Tourism Guide: Joyo City Kutsukawa Kofun Cluster] Many kofun have been lost or obscured due to recent residential development.[https://bunka.nii.ac.jp/heritages/detail/138764 Cultural Heritage Online: Kutsukawa Kurazuka and Marutsuka Kofun] Previously, {{ill|Kutsukawa Kurazuka Kofun|ja|久津川車塚古墳}} and {{ill|Maruzuka Kofun (Jōyō City)|ja|丸塚古墳 (城陽市)}} were designated collectively as the National Historic Site "Kutsukawa Kurazuka and Marutsuka Kofun." In 2016, {{ill|Basho-zuka Kofun|ja|芭蕉塚古墳}} and {{ill|Kuse Elementary School Kofun|ja|久世小学校古墳}} were added to the designation, and the name was changed to "Kutsukawa Kofun Cluster."{{PDFlink|[https://www.bunka.go.jp/koho_hodo_oshirase/hodohappyo/pdf/2016061701_besshi03.pdf Regarding Designations of Historic Sites]}} (Agency for Cultural Affairs, June 17, 2016).Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology Notification No. 144, October 3, 2016. Separately, Shibagahara No. 12 Kofun has been designated as the National Historic Site "{{ill|Shibagahara Kofun|ja|芝ヶ原古墳}}" and is not part of the "Kutsukawa Kofun Cluster." == Major Kofun == * **{{ill|Kutsukawa Kurazuka Kofun|ja|久津川車塚古墳}}** - National Historic Site. The largest keyhole-shaped kofun in the cluster and one of the largest in the Yamashiro region. A {{ill|Nagashigata stone coffin|ja|長持形石棺}} made of Ryuzan stone was discovered here. * **{{ill|Maruzuka Kofun (Jōyō City)|ja|丸塚古墳 (城陽市)}}** - National Historic Site. Keyhole-shaped kofun. * **Kajizuka Kofun** - Square burial mound partially overlapping Kutsukawa Kurazuka Kofun. * **Shigetsuzuka Kofun** - Round burial mound previously located on the grounds of {{ill|Joyo Municipal Kutsukawa Elementary School|ja|城陽市立久津川小学校}} but now lost due to construction. * **Hakozuka Kofun** - Keyhole-shaped kofun. * **Yamamichi Kofun** - Square burial mound lost due to residential development. * **{{ill|Shibagahara Kofun Group|ja|芝ヶ原古墳群}}** - A group of 13 kofun. Shibagahara No. 12 Kofun is designated as the National Historic Site "{{ill|Shibagahara Kofun|ja|芝ヶ原古墳}}," while Shibagahara No. 9 Kofun, located in the courtyard of {{ill|Joyo Municipal Kuse Elementary School|ja|城陽市立久世小学校}}, is designated as "{{ill|Kuse Elementary School Kofun|ja|久世小学校古墳}}." * **{{ill|Nitsuka Kofun Group|ja|尼塚古墳群}}** - A group of seven kofun. Part of the cluster is designated as a National Historic Site and represents one of the largest kofun groups in Kyoto Prefecture.[http://mj-ktmr2.digi2.jp/p26ky/pys26207kutugawa.htm Kofun of Joyo City] == Overview == The Kutsukawa Kofun Cluster is situated in the lowlands and hills surrounding the Otanigawa River, east of {{ill|Kintetsu|ja|近畿日本鉄道}}'s Kutsukawa Station. Narrowly defined, the cluster includes around ten kofun near {{ill|Kutsukawa Kurazuka Kofun|ja|久津川車塚古墳}}, but when including smaller kofun scattered throughout the nearby hills, the total number of burial mounds is estimated to be around 150.[http://www.kyoto-kankou.or.jp/info_search/?id=379&r=1441389345.907 Kyoto Tourism Guide: Joyo City Kutsukawa Kofun Cluster] Many kofun have been lost or obscured due to recent residential development.[https://bunka.nii.ac.jp/heritages/detail/138764 Cultural Heritage Online: Kutsukawa Kurazuka and Marutsuka Kofun] Previously, {{ill|Kutsukawa Kurazuka Kofun|ja|久津川車塚古墳}} and {{ill|Maruzuka Kofun (Jōyō City)|ja|丸塚古墳 (城陽市)}} were designated collectively as the National Historic Site "Kutsukawa Kurazuka and Marutsuka Kofun." In 2016, {{ill|Basho-zuka Kofun|ja|芭蕉塚古墳}} and {{ill|Kuse Elementary School Kofun|ja|久世小学校古墳}} were added to the designation, and the name was changed to "Kutsukawa Kofun Cluster."{{PDFlink|[https://www.bunka.go.jp/koho_hodo_oshirase/hodohappyo/pdf/2016061701_besshi03.pdf Regarding Designations of Historic Sites]}} (Agency for Cultural Affairs, June 17, 2016).Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology Notification No. 144, October 3, 2016. Separately, Shibagahara No. 12 Kofun has been designated as the National Historic Site "{{ill|Shibagahara Kofun|ja|芝ヶ原古墳}}" and is not part of the "Kutsukawa Kofun Cluster." == Major Kofun == * **{{ill|Kutsukawa Kurazuka Kofun|ja|久津川車塚古墳}}** - National Historic Site. Shibagahara No. 12 Kofun is designated as the National Historic Site "{{ill|Shibagahara Kofun|ja|芝ヶ原古墳}}," while Shibagahara No. 9 Kofun, located in the courtyard of {{ill|Joyo Municipal Kuse Elementary School|ja|城陽市立久世小学校}}, is designated as "{{ill|Kuse Elementary School Kofun|ja|久世小学校古墳}}." * **{{ill|Nitsuka Kofun Group|ja|尼塚古墳群}}** - A group of seven kofun. {{Location map|Japan Kyoto|lat_deg=34|lat_min=51|lat_sec=53.32|lon_deg=135|lon_min=46|lon_sec=44.19|label=Kutsukawa
Kofun Cluster|position=top|width=220|Red pog.svg|marksize=10|caption={{center|Location of the Kutsukawa Kofun Cluster}}}} '''Kutsukawa Kofun Cluster''' (久津川古墳群) is a group of [[kofun]] burial mounds located in {{ill|Joyo|ja|城陽市}}, Kyoto Prefecture, Japan. Part of the cluster is designated as a National Historic Site and represents one of the largest kofun groups in Kyoto Prefecture.[http://mj-ktmr2.digi2.jp/p26ky/pys26207kutugawa.htm Kofun of Joyo City] == Overview == The Kutsukawa Kofun Cluster is situated in the lowlands and hills surrounding the Otanigawa River, east of {{ill|Kintetsu|ja|近畿日本鉄道}}'s Kutsukawa Station. Narrowly defined, the cluster includes around ten kofun near {{ill|Kutsukawa Kurazuka Kofun|ja|久津川車塚古墳}}, but when including smaller kofun scattered throughout the nearby hills, the total number of burial mounds is estimated to be around 150.[http://www.kyoto-kankou.or.jp/info_search/?id=379&r=1441389345.907 Kyoto Tourism Guide: Joyo City Kutsukawa Kofun Cluster] Many kofun have been lost or obscured due to recent residential development.[https://bunka.nii.ac.jp/heritages/detail/138764 Cultural Heritage Online: Kutsukawa Kurazuka and Marutsuka Kofun] Previously, {{ill|Kutsukawa Kurazuka Kofun|ja|久津川車塚古墳}} and {{ill|Maruzuka Kofun (Jōyō City)|ja|丸塚古墳 (城陽市)}} were designated collectively as the National Historic Site "Kutsukawa Kurazuka and Marutsuka Kofun." In 2016, {{ill|Basho-zuka Kofun|ja|芭蕉塚古墳}} and {{ill|Kuse Elementary School Kofun|ja|久世小学校古墳}} were added to the designation, and the name was changed to "Kutsukawa Kofun Cluster."{{PDFlink|[https://www.bunka.go.jp/koho_hodo_oshirase/hodohappyo/pdf/2016061701_besshi03.pdf Regarding Designations of Historic Sites]}} (Agency for Cultural Affairs, June 17, 2016).Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology Notification No. 144, October 3, 2016. Separately, Shibagahara No. 12 Kofun has been designated as the National Historic Site "{{ill|Shibagahara Kofun|ja|芝ヶ原古墳}}" and is not part of the "Kutsukawa Kofun Cluster." == Major Kofun == * **{{ill|Kutsukawa Kurazuka Kofun|ja|久津川車塚古墳}}** - National Historic Site. The largest keyhole-shaped kofun in the cluster and one of the largest in the Yamashiro region. A {{ill|Nagashigata stone coffin|ja|長持形石棺}} made of Ryuzan stone was discovered here. * **{{ill|Maruzuka Kofun (Jōyō City)|ja|丸塚古墳 (城陽市)}}** - National Historic Site. A scallop-shaped kofun. * **{{ill|Aotsuka Kofun|ja|青塚古墳 (城陽市)}}** - Rectangular front and rear burial mound. * **{{ill|Akatsuka Kofun|ja|赤塚古墳 (城陽市)}}** - Round burial mound adjacent to {{ill|Hirakawa Temple Ruins|ja|平川廃寺跡}}. * **{{ill|Basho-zuka Kofun|ja|芭蕉塚古墳}}** - National Historic Site. Keyhole-shaped kofun. * **Kajizuka Kofun** - Square burial mound partially overlapping Kutsukawa Kurazuka Kofun. * **Shigetsuzuka Kofun** - Round burial mound previously located on the grounds of {{ill|Joyo Municipal Kutsukawa Elementary School|ja|城陽市立久津川小学校}} but now lost due to construction. * **Hakozuka Kofun** - Keyhole-shaped kofun. * **Yamamichi Kofun** - Square burial mound lost due to residential development. * **{{ill|Shibagahara Kofun Group|ja|芝ヶ原古墳群}}** - A group of 13 kofun. Shibagahara No. 12 Kofun is designated as the National Historic Site "{{ill|Shibagahara Kofun|ja|芝ヶ原古墳}}," while Shibagahara No. 9 Kofun, located in the courtyard of {{ill|Joyo Municipal Kuse Elementary School|ja|城陽市立久世小学校}}, is designated as "{{ill|Kuse Elementary School Kofun|ja|久世小学校古墳}}." * **{{ill|Nitsuka Kofun Group|ja|尼塚古墳群}}** - A group of seven kofun. Nos. 1–5 have been lost, while Nos. 6 and 7 are preserved. * **Kami-Otani Kofun Group** - A group of 20 kofun, with 11 preserved. * **Shimo-Otani Kofun Group** - A group of two kofun. No. 2 has been lost, while No. 1 is preserved. * **{{ill|Nishiyama Kofun Group|ja|西山古墳群 (城陽市)}}** - Formerly near the Shimo-Otani group but lost due to residential development. * **Otakeshi Kofun** - Square burial mound. * **{{ill|Anjiyama Kofun|ja|庵寺山古墳}}** - Round burial mound. == Other Sites == * **{{ill|Hirakawa Temple Ruins|ja|平川廃寺跡}}** - National Historic Site adjacent to Akatsuka Kofun. * **{{ill|Kuse Temple Ruins|ja|久世廃寺跡}}** - National Historic Site. * **{{ill|Seido Administrative Complex Ruins|ja|正道官衙遺跡}}** - National Historic Site. == Cultural Properties == === Important Cultural Properties (National Designation) === * **Mirrors excavated from Kutsukawa Kurazuka Kofun (7 pieces, archaeological artifacts)** - Stored at {{ill|Sen-oku Hakukokan Museum|ja|泉屋博古館}}. Designated on November 14, 1953.{{National Cultural Property Database|201|9721|Mirrors Excavated from Kutsukawa Kurazuka Kofun}} * **Artifacts excavated from Shibagahara Kofun in Kyoto Prefecture (archaeological artifacts)** - Stored at Joyo City Historical Museum. Designated on June 29, 1990.{{National Cultural Property Database|201|10078|Artifacts Excavated from Shibagahara Kofun}} * **Nagashigata Stone Coffin excavated from Kutsukawa Kurazuka Kofun (archaeological artifacts)** - Stored at Kyoto University. Designated on June 21, 1991.{{National Cultural Property Database|201|10083|Nagashigata Stone Coffin Excavated from Kutsukawa Kurazuka Kofun}} === National Historic Sites === * **Kutsukawa Kofun Cluster** ** Kutsukawa Kurazuka Kofun ** Marutsuka Kofun ** Basho-zuka Kofun ** Kuse Elementary School Kofun *: Designated on January 19, 1979, as "Kutsukawa Kurazuka and Marutsuka Kofun." *: Renamed "Kutsukawa Kofun Cluster" with the inclusion of Basho-zuka and Kuse Elementary School Kofun on October 3, 2016.{{National Cultural Property Database|401|1741|Kutsukawa Kofun Cluster}} * **Shibagahara Kofun** *: Designated on September 6, 1989. *: Boundary expanded on January 24, 2012.{{National Cultural Property Database|401|1750|Shibagahara Kofun}} === Joyo City Designated Cultural Properties === * **Artifacts Excavated from Shibagahara No. 11 Kofun (archaeological artifacts)** File:芝ヶ原11号墳出土 三角縁銘帯三神四獣鏡.JPG|Triangular-rimmed mirror excavated from Shibagahara No. 11 Kofun

Kofun Cluster|position=top|width=220|Red pog.svg|marksize=10|caption={{center|Location of the Kutsukawa Kofun Cluster}}}} '''Kutsukawa Kofun Cluster''' (久津川古墳群) is a group of [[kofun]] burial mounds located in {{ill|Joyo|ja|城陽市}}, Kyoto Prefecture, Japan. Part of the cluster is designated as a National Historic Site and represents one of the largest kofun groups in Kyoto Prefecture.[http://mj-ktmr2.digi2.jp/p26ky/pys26207kutugawa.htm Kofun of Joyo City] == Overview == The Kutsukawa Kofun Cluster is situated in the lowlands and hills surrounding the Otanigawa River, east of {{ill|Kintetsu|ja|近畿日本鉄道}}'s Kutsukawa Station. Narrowly defined, the cluster includes around ten kofun near {{ill|Kutsukawa Kurazuka Kofun|ja|久津川車塚古墳}}, but when including smaller kofun scattered throughout the nearby hills, the total number of burial mounds is estimated to be around 150.[http://www.kyoto-kankou.or.jp/info_search/?id=379&r=1441389345.907 Kyoto Tourism Guide: Joyo City Kutsukawa Kofun Cluster] Many kofun have been lost or obscured due to recent residential development.[https://bunka.nii.ac.jp/heritages/detail/138764 Cultural Heritage Online: Kutsukawa Kurazuka and Marutsuka Kofun] Previously, {{ill|Kutsukawa Kurazuka Kofun|ja|久津川車塚古墳}} and {{ill|Maruzuka Kofun (Jōyō City)|ja|丸塚古墳 (城陽市)}} were designated collectively as the National Historic Site "Kutsukawa Kurazuka and Marutsuka Kofun." In 2016, {{ill|Basho-zuka Kofun|ja|芭蕉塚古墳}} and {{ill|Kuse Elementary School Kofun|ja|久世小学校古墳}} were added to the designation, and the name was changed to "Kutsukawa Kofun Cluster."{{PDFlink|[https://www.bunka.go.jp/koho_hodo_oshirase/hodohappyo/pdf/2016061701_besshi03.pdf Regarding Designations of Historic Sites]}} (Agency for Cultural Affairs, June 17, 2016).Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology Notification No. 144, October 3, 2016. Separately, Shibagahara No. 12 Kofun has been designated as the National Historic Site "{{ill|Shibagahara Kofun|ja|芝ヶ原古墳}}" and is not part of the "Kutsukawa Kofun Cluster." == Major Kofun == * **{{ill|Kutsukawa Kurazuka Kofun|ja|久津川車塚古墳}}** - National Historic Site. The largest keyhole-shaped kofun in the cluster and one of the largest in the Yamashiro region. A {{ill|Nagashigata stone coffin|ja|長持形石棺}} made of Ryuzan stone was discovered here. * **{{ill|Maruzuka Kofun (Jōyō City)|ja|丸塚古墳 (城陽市)}}** - National Historic Site. A scallop-shaped kofun. * **{{ill|Aotsuka Kofun|ja|青塚古墳 (城陽市)}}** - Rectangular front and rear burial mound. * **{{ill|Akatsuka Kofun|ja|赤塚古墳 (城陽市)}}** - Round burial mound adjacent to {{ill|Hirakawa Temple Ruins|ja|平川廃寺跡}}. * **{{ill|Basho-zuka Kofun|ja|芭蕉塚古墳}}** - National Historic Site. Keyhole-shaped kofun. * **Kajizuka Kofun** - Square burial mound partially overlapping Kutsukawa Kurazuka Kofun. * **Shigetsuzuka Kofun** - Round burial mound previously located on the grounds of {{ill|Joyo Municipal Kutsukawa Elementary School|ja|城陽市立久津川小学校}} but now lost due to construction. * **Hakozuka Kofun** - Keyhole-shaped kofun. * **Yamamichi Kofun** - Square burial mound lost due to residential development. * **{{ill|Shibagahara Kofun Group|ja|芝ヶ原古墳群}}** - A group of 13 kofun. Shibagahara No. 12 Kofun is designated as the National Historic Site "{{ill|Shibagahara Kofun|ja|芝ヶ原古墳}}," while Shibagahara No. 9 Kofun, located in the courtyard of {{ill|Joyo Municipal Kuse Elementary School|ja|城陽市立久世小学校}}, is designated as "{{ill|Kuse Elementary School Kofun|ja|久世小学校古墳}}." * **{{ill|Nitsuka Kofun Group|ja|尼塚古墳群}}** - A group of seven kofun. Nos. 1–5 have been lost, while Nos. 6 and 7 are preserved. * **Kami-Otani Kofun Group** - A group of 20 kofun, with 11 preserved. * **Shimo-Otani Kofun Group** - A group of two kofun. Kofun Cluster|position=top|width=220|Red pog.svg|marksize=10|caption={{center|Location of the Kutsukawa Kofun Cluster}}}} '''Kutsukawa Kofun Cluster''' (久津川古墳群) is a group of [[kofun]] burial mounds located in {{ill|Joyo|ja|城陽市}}, Kyoto Prefecture, Japan. Part of the cluster is designated as a National Historic Site and represents one of the largest kofun groups in Kyoto Prefecture.[http://mj-ktmr2.digi2.jp/p26ky/pys26207kutugawa.htm Kofun of Joyo City] == Overview == The Kutsukawa Kofun Cluster is situated in the lowlands and hills surrounding the Otanigawa River, east of {{ill|Kintetsu|ja|近畿日本鉄道}}'s Kutsukawa Station. Narrowly defined, the cluster includes around ten kofun near {{ill|Kutsukawa Kurazuka Kofun|ja|久津川車塚古墳}}, but when including smaller kofun scattered throughout the nearby hills, the total number of burial mounds is estimated to be around 150.[http://www.kyoto-kankou.or.jp/info_search/?id=379&r=1441389345.907 Kyoto Tourism Guide: Joyo City Kutsukawa Kofun Cluster] Many kofun have been lost or obscured due to recent residential development.[https://bunka.nii.ac.jp/heritages/detail/138764 Cultural Heritage Online: Kutsukawa Kurazuka and Marutsuka Kofun] Previously, {{ill|Kutsukawa Kurazuka Kofun|ja|久津川車塚古墳}} and {{ill|Maruzuka Kofun (Jōyō City)|ja|丸塚古墳 (城陽市)}} were designated collectively as the National Historic Site "Kutsukawa Kurazuka and Marutsuka Kofun." In 2016, {{ill|Basho-zuka Kofun|ja|芭蕉塚古墳}} and {{ill|Kuse Elementary School Kofun|ja|久世小学校古墳}} were added to the designation, and the name was changed to "Kutsukawa Kofun Cluster."{{PDFlink|[https://www.bunka.go.jp/koho_hodo_oshirase/hodohappyo/pdf/2016061701_besshi03.pdf Regarding Designations of Historic Sites]}} (Agency for Cultural Affairs, June 17, 2016).Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology Notification No. 144, October 3, 2016. Separately, Shibagahara No. 12 Kofun has been designated as the National Historic Site "{{ill|Shibagahara Kofun|ja|芝ヶ原古墳}}" and is not part of the "Kutsukawa Kofun Cluster." == Major Kofun == * **{{ill|Kutsukawa Kurazuka Kofun|ja|久津川車塚古墳}}** - National Historic Site. The largest keyhole-shaped kofun in the cluster and one of the largest in the Yamashiro region. A {{ill|Nagashigata stone coffin|ja|長持形石棺}} made of Ryuzan stone was discovered here. * **{{ill|Maruzuka Kofun (Jōyō City)|ja|丸塚古墳 (城陽市)}}** - National Historic Site. A scallop-shaped kofun. * **{{ill|Aotsuka Kofun|ja|青塚古墳 (城陽市)}}** - Rectangular front and rear burial mound. * **{{ill|Akatsuka Kofun|ja|赤塚古墳 (城陽市)}}** - Round burial mound adjacent to {{ill|Hirakawa Temple Ruins|ja|平川廃寺跡}}. * **{{ill|Basho-zuka Kofun|ja|芭蕉塚古墳}}** - National Historic Site. Keyhole-shaped kofun. * **Kajizuka Kofun** - Square burial mound partially overlapping Kutsukawa Kurazuka Kofun. * **Shigetsuzuka Kofun** - Round burial mound previously located on the grounds of {{ill|Joyo Municipal Kutsukawa Elementary School|ja|城陽市立久津川小学校}} but now lost due to construction. * **Hakozuka Kofun** - Keyhole-shaped kofun. * **Yamamichi Kofun** - Square burial mound lost due to residential development. * **{{ill|Shibagahara Kofun Group|ja|芝ヶ原古墳群}}** - A group of 13 kofun. Shibagahara No. 12 Kofun is designated as the National Historic Site "{{ill|Shibagahara Kofun|ja|芝ヶ原古墳}}," while Shibagahara No. 9 Kofun, located in the courtyard of {{ill|Joyo Municipal Kuse Elementary School|ja|城陽市立久世小学校}}, is designated as "{{ill|Kuse Elementary School Kofun|ja|久世小学校古墳}}." * **{{ill|Nitsuka Kofun Group|ja|尼塚古墳群}}** - A group of seven kofun. Nos. 1–5 have been lost, while Nos. 6 and 7 are preserved. * **Kami-Otani Kofun Group** - A group of 20 kofun, with 11 preserved. * **Shimo-Otani Kofun Group** - A group of two kofun. No. 2 has been lost, while No. 1 is preserved. * **{{ill|Nishiyama Kofun Group|ja|西山古墳群 (城陽市)}}** - Formerly near the Shimo-Otani group but lost due to residential development. * **Otakeshi Kofun** - Square burial mound. * **{{ill|Anjiyama Kofun|ja|庵寺山古墳}}** - Round burial mound. == Other Sites == * **{{ill|Hirakawa Temple Ruins|ja|平川廃寺跡}}** - National Historic Site adjacent to Akatsuka Kofun. * **{{ill|Kuse Temple Ruins|ja|久世廃寺跡}}** - National Historic Site. * **{{ill|Seido Administrative Complex Ruins|ja|正道官衙遺跡}}** - National Historic Site. == Cultural Properties == === Important Cultural Properties (National Designation) === * **Mirrors excavated from Kutsukawa Kurazuka Kofun (7 pieces, archaeological artifacts)** - Stored at {{ill|Sen-oku Hakukokan Museum|ja|泉屋博古館}}. Designated on November 14, 1953.{{National Cultural Property Database|201|9721|Mirrors Excavated from Kutsukawa Kurazuka Kofun}} * **Artifacts excavated from Shibagahara Kofun in Kyoto Prefecture (archaeological artifacts)** - Stored at Joyo City Historical Museum. Designated on June 29, 1990.{{National Cultural Property Database|201|10078|Artifacts Excavated from Shibagahara Kofun}} * **Nagashigata Stone Coffin excavated from Kutsukawa Kurazuka Kofun (archaeological artifacts)** - Stored at Kyoto University. Part of the cluster is designated as a National Historic Site and represents one of the largest kofun groups in Kyoto Prefecture.[http://mj-ktmr2.digi2.jp/p26ky/pys26207kutugawa.htm Kofun of Joyo City] == Overview == The Kutsukawa Kofun Cluster is situated in the lowlands and hills surrounding the Otanigawa River, east of {{ill|Kintetsu|ja|近畿日本鉄道}}'s Kutsukawa Station. Narrowly defined, the cluster includes around ten kofun near {{ill|Kutsukawa Kurazuka Kofun|ja|久津川車塚古墳}}, but when including smaller kofun scattered throughout the nearby hills, the total number of burial mounds is estimated to be around 150.[http://www.kyoto-kankou.or.jp/info_search/?id=379&r=1441389345.907 Kyoto Tourism Guide: Joyo City Kutsukawa Kofun Cluster] Many kofun have been lost or obscured due to recent residential development.[https://bunka.nii.ac.jp/heritages/detail/138764 Cultural Heritage Online: Kutsukawa Kurazuka and Marutsuka Kofun] Previously, {{ill|Kutsukawa Kurazuka Kofun|ja|久津川車塚古墳}} and {{ill|Maruzuka Kofun (Jōyō City)|ja|丸塚古墳 (城陽市)}} were designated collectively as the National Historic Site "Kutsukawa Kurazuka and Marutsuka Kofun." In 2016, {{ill|Basho-zuka Kofun|ja|芭蕉塚古墳}} and {{ill|Kuse Elementary School Kofun|ja|久世小学校古墳}} were added to the designation, and the name was changed to "Kutsukawa Kofun Cluster."{{PDFlink|[https://www.bunka.go.jp/koho_hodo_oshirase/hodohappyo/pdf/2016061701_besshi03.pdf Regarding Designations of Historic Sites]}} (Agency for Cultural Affairs, June 17, 2016).Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology Notification No. 144, October 3, 2016. Separately, Shibagahara No. 12 Kofun has been designated as the National Historic Site "{{ill|Shibagahara Kofun|ja|芝ヶ原古墳}}" and is not part of the "Kutsukawa Kofun Cluster." == Major Kofun == * **{{ill|Kutsukawa Kurazuka Kofun|ja|久津川車塚古墳}}** - National Historic Site. Kofun Cluster|position=top|width=220|Red pog.svg|marksize=10|caption={{center|Location of the Kutsukawa Kofun Cluster}}}} '''Kutsukawa Kofun Cluster''' (久津川古墳群) is a group of [[kofun]] burial mounds located in {{ill|Joyo|ja|城陽市}}, Kyoto Prefecture, Japan. Part of the cluster is designated as a National Historic Site and represents one of the largest kofun groups in Kyoto Prefecture.[http://mj-ktmr2.digi2.jp/p26ky/pys26207kutugawa.htm Kofun of Joyo City] == Overview == The Kutsukawa Kofun Cluster is situated in the lowlands and hills surrounding the Otanigawa River, east of {{ill|Kintetsu|ja|近畿日本鉄道}}'s Kutsukawa Station. Narrowly defined, the cluster includes around ten kofun near {{ill|Kutsukawa Kurazuka Kofun|ja|久津川車塚古墳}}, but when including smaller kofun scattered throughout the nearby hills, the total number of burial mounds is estimated to be around 150.[http://www.kyoto-kankou.or.jp/info_search/?id=379&r=1441389345.907 Kyoto Tourism Guide: Joyo City Kutsukawa Kofun Cluster] Many kofun have been lost or obscured due to recent residential development.[https://bunka.nii.ac.jp/heritages/detail/138764 Cultural Heritage Online: Kutsukawa Kurazuka and Marutsuka Kofun] Previously, {{ill|Kutsukawa Kurazuka Kofun|ja|久津川車塚古墳}} and {{ill|Maruzuka Kofun (Jōyō City)|ja|丸塚古墳 (城陽市)}} were designated collectively as the National Historic Site "Kutsukawa Kurazuka and Marutsuka Kofun." In 2016, {{ill|Basho-zuka Kofun|ja|芭蕉塚古墳}} and {{ill|Kuse Elementary School Kofun|ja|久世小学校古墳}} were added to the designation, and the name was changed to "Kutsukawa Kofun Cluster."{{PDFlink|[https://www.bunka.go.jp/koho_hodo_oshirase/hodohappyo/pdf/2016061701_besshi03.pdf Regarding Designations of Historic Sites]}} (Agency for Cultural Affairs, June 17, 2016).Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology Notification No. 144, October 3, 2016. Separately, Shibagahara No. 12 Kofun has been designated as the National Historic Site "{{ill|Shibagahara Kofun|ja|芝ヶ原古墳}}" and is not part of the "Kutsukawa Kofun Cluster." == Major Kofun == * **{{ill|Kutsukawa Kurazuka Kofun|ja|久津川車塚古墳}}** - National Historic Site. The largest keyhole-shaped kofun in the cluster and one of the largest in the Yamashiro region. A {{ill|Nagashigata stone coffin|ja|長持形石棺}} made of Ryuzan stone was discovered here. * **{{ill|Maruzuka Kofun (Jōyō City)|ja|丸塚古墳 (城陽市)}}** - National Historic Site. A scallop-shaped kofun. * **{{ill|Aotsuka Kofun|ja|青塚古墳 (城陽市)}}** - Rectangular front and rear burial mound. * **{{ill|Akatsuka Kofun|ja|赤塚古墳 (城陽市)}}** - Round burial mound adjacent to {{ill|Hirakawa Temple Ruins|ja|平川廃寺跡}}. * **{{ill|Basho-zuka Kofun|ja|芭蕉塚古墳}}** - National Historic Site. Keyhole-shaped kofun. * **Kajizuka Kofun** - Square burial mound partially overlapping Kutsukawa Kurazuka Kofun. * **Shigetsuzuka Kofun** - Round burial mound previously located on the grounds of {{ill|Joyo Municipal Kutsukawa Elementary School|ja|城陽市立久津川小学校}} but now lost due to construction. * **Hakozuka Kofun** - Keyhole-shaped kofun. * **Yamamichi Kofun** - Square burial mound lost due to residential development. * **{{ill|Shibagahara Kofun Group|ja|芝ヶ原古墳群}}** - A group of 13 kofun. Shibagahara No. 12 Kofun is designated as the National Historic Site "{{ill|Shibagahara Kofun|ja|芝ヶ原古墳}}," while Shibagahara No. 9 Kofun, located in the courtyard of {{ill|Joyo Municipal Kuse Elementary School|ja|城陽市立久世小学校}}, is designated as "{{ill|Kuse Elementary School Kofun|ja|久世小学校古墳}}." * **{{ill|Nitsuka Kofun Group|ja|尼塚古墳群}}** - A group of seven kofun. Nos. 1–5 have been lost, while Nos. 6 and 7 are preserved. * **Kami-Otani Kofun Group** - A group of 20 kofun, with 11 preserved. * **Shimo-Otani Kofun Group** - A group of two kofun. No. 2 has been lost, while No. 1 is preserved. * **{{ill|Nishiyama Kofun Group|ja|西山古墳群 (城陽市)}}** - Formerly near the Shimo-Otani group but lost due to residential development. * **Otakeshi Kofun** - Square burial mound. * **{{ill|Anjiyama Kofun|ja|庵寺山古墳}}** - Round burial mound. == Other Sites == * **{{ill|Hirakawa Temple Ruins|ja|平川廃寺跡}}** - National Historic Site adjacent to Akatsuka Kofun. * **{{ill|Kuse Temple Ruins|ja|久世廃寺跡}}** - National Historic Site. * **{{ill|Seido Administrative Complex Ruins|ja|正道官衙遺跡}}** - National Historic Site. == Cultural Properties == === Important Cultural Properties (National Designation) === * **Mirrors excavated from Kutsukawa Kurazuka Kofun (7 pieces, archaeological artifacts)** - Stored at {{ill|Sen-oku Hakukokan Museum|ja|泉屋博古館}}. {{Location map|Japan Kyoto|lat_deg=34|lat_min=51|lat_sec=53.32|lon_deg=135|lon_min=46|lon_sec=44.19|label=Kutsukawa
Kofun Cluster|position=top|width=220|Red pog.svg|marksize=10|caption={{center|Location of the Kutsukawa Kofun Cluster}}}} '''Kutsukawa Kofun Cluster''' (久津川古墳群) is a group of [[kofun]] burial mounds located in {{ill|Joyo|ja|城陽市}}, Kyoto Prefecture, Japan. Part of the cluster is designated as a National Historic Site and represents one of the largest kofun groups in Kyoto Prefecture.[http://mj-ktmr2.digi2.jp/p26ky/pys26207kutugawa.htm Kofun of Joyo City] == Overview == The Kutsukawa Kofun Cluster is situated in the lowlands and hills surrounding the Otanigawa River, east of {{ill|Kintetsu|ja|近畿日本鉄道}}'s Kutsukawa Station. Narrowly defined, the cluster includes around ten kofun near {{ill|Kutsukawa Kurazuka Kofun|ja|久津川車塚古墳}}, but when including smaller kofun scattered throughout the nearby hills, the total number of burial mounds is estimated to be around 150.[http://www.kyoto-kankou.or.jp/info_search/?id=379&r=1441389345.907 Kyoto Tourism Guide: Joyo City Kutsukawa Kofun Cluster] Many kofun have been lost or obscured due to recent residential development.[https://bunka.nii.ac.jp/heritages/detail/138764 Cultural Heritage Online: Kutsukawa Kurazuka and Marutsuka Kofun] Previously, {{ill|Kutsukawa Kurazuka Kofun|ja|久津川車塚古墳}} and {{ill|Maruzuka Kofun (Jōyō City)|ja|丸塚古墳 (城陽市)}} were designated collectively as the National Historic Site "Kutsukawa Kurazuka and Marutsuka Kofun." In 2016, {{ill|Basho-zuka Kofun|ja|芭蕉塚古墳}} and {{ill|Kuse Elementary School Kofun|ja|久世小学校古墳}} were added to the designation, and the name was changed to "Kutsukawa Kofun Cluster."{{PDFlink|[https://www.bunka.go.jp/koho_hodo_oshirase/hodohappyo/pdf/2016061701_besshi03.pdf Regarding Designations of Historic Sites]}} (Agency for Cultural Affairs, June 17, 2016).Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology Notification No. 144, October 3, 2016. Separately, Shibagahara No. 12 Kofun has been designated as the National Historic Site "{{ill|Shibagahara Kofun|ja|芝ヶ原古墳}}" and is not part of the "Kutsukawa Kofun Cluster." == Major Kofun == * **{{ill|Kutsukawa Kurazuka Kofun|ja|久津川車塚古墳}}** - National Historic Site. The largest keyhole-shaped kofun in the cluster and one of the largest in the Yamashiro region. A {{ill|Nagashigata stone coffin|ja|長持形石棺}} made of Ryuzan stone was discovered here. * **{{ill|Maruzuka Kofun (Jōyō City)|ja|丸塚古墳 (城陽市)}}** - National Historic Site. A scallop-shaped kofun. * **{{ill|Aotsuka Kofun|ja|青塚古墳 (城陽市)}}** - Rectangular front and rear burial mound. * **{{ill|Akatsuka Kofun|ja|赤塚古墳 (城陽市)}}** - Round burial mound adjacent to {{ill|Hirakawa Temple Ruins|ja|平川廃寺跡}}. * **{{ill|Basho-zuka Kofun|ja|芭蕉塚古墳}}** - National Historic Site. Keyhole-shaped kofun. * **Kajizuka Kofun** - Square burial mound partially overlapping Kutsukawa Kurazuka Kofun. * **Shigetsuzuka Kofun** - Round burial mound previously located on the grounds of {{ill|Joyo Municipal Kutsukawa Elementary School|ja|城陽市立久津川小学校}} but now lost due to construction. * **Hakozuka Kofun** - Keyhole-shaped kofun. * **Yamamichi Kofun** - Square burial mound lost due to residential development. * **{{ill|Shibagahara Kofun Group|ja|芝ヶ原古墳群}}** - A group of 13 kofun. Shibagahara No. 12 Kofun is designated as the National Historic Site "{{ill|Shibagahara Kofun|ja|芝ヶ原古墳}}," while Shibagahara No. 9 Kofun, located in the courtyard of {{ill|Joyo Municipal Kuse Elementary School|ja|城陽市立久世小学校}}, is designated as "{{ill|Kuse Elementary School Kofun|ja|久世小学校古墳}}." * **{{ill|Nitsuka Kofun Group|ja|尼塚古墳群}}** - A group of seven kofun. Nos. 1–5 have been lost, while Nos. 6 and 7 are preserved. * **Kami-Otani Kofun Group** - A group of 20 kofun, with 11 preserved. * **Shimo-Otani Kofun Group** - A group of two kofun. No. 2 has been lost, while No. 1 is preserved. * **{{ill|Nishiyama Kofun Group|ja|西山古墳群 (城陽市)}}** - Formerly near the Shimo-Otani group but lost due to residential development. * **Otakeshi Kofun** - Square burial mound. * **{{ill|Anjiyama Kofun|ja|庵寺山古墳}}** - Round burial mound. == Other Sites == * **{{ill|Hirakawa Temple Ruins|ja|平川廃寺跡}}** - National Historic Site adjacent to Akatsuka Kofun. * **{{ill|Kuse Temple Ruins|ja|久世廃寺跡}}** - National Historic Site. * **{{ill|Seido Administrative Complex Ruins|ja|正道官衙遺跡}}** - National Historic Site. == Cultural Properties == === Important Cultural Properties (National Designation) === * **Mirrors excavated from Kutsukawa Kurazuka Kofun (7 pieces, archaeological artifacts)** - Stored at {{ill|Sen-oku Hakukokan Museum|ja|泉屋博古館}}. Designated on November 14, 1953.{{National Cultural Property Database|201|9721|Mirrors Excavated from Kutsukawa Kurazuka Kofun}} * **Artifacts excavated from Shibagahara Kofun in Kyoto Prefecture (archaeological artifacts)** - Stored at Joyo City Historical Museum. Designated on June 29, 1990.{{National Cultural Property Database|201|10078|Artifacts Excavated from Shibagahara Kofun}} * **Nagashigata Stone Coffin excavated from Kutsukawa Kurazuka Kofun (archaeological artifacts)** - Stored at Kyoto University. Designated on June 21, 1991.{{National Cultural Property Database|201|10083|Nagashigata Stone Coffin Excavated from Kutsukawa Kurazuka Kofun}} === National Historic Sites === * **Kutsukawa Kofun Cluster** ** Kutsukawa Kurazuka Kofun ** Marutsuka Kofun ** Basho-zuka Kofun ** Kuse Elementary School Kofun *: Designated on January 19, 1979, as "Kutsukawa Kurazuka and Marutsuka Kofun." *: Renamed "Kutsukawa Kofun Cluster" with the inclusion of Basho-zuka and Kuse Elementary School Kofun on October 3, 2016.{{National Cultural Property Database|401|1741|Kutsukawa Kofun Cluster}} * **Shibagahara Kofun** *: Designated on September 6, 1989. *: Boundary expanded on January 24, 2012.{{National Cultural Property Database|401|1750|Shibagahara Kofun}} === Joyo City Designated Cultural Properties === * **Artifacts Excavated from Shibagahara No. 11 Kofun (archaeological artifacts)** File:芝ヶ原11号墳出土 三角縁銘帯三神四獣鏡.JPG|Triangular-rimmed mirror excavated from Shibagahara No. 11 Kofun
{{small|Exhibited at the Joyo City Historical Museum (Gorikan).}} == Access == * Approximately 10–45 minutes on foot from {{ill|Kintetsu|ja|近畿日本鉄道}} Kutsukawa Station. * Approximately 10–45 minutes on {{Location map|Japan Kyoto|lat_deg=34|lat_min=51|lat_sec=53.32|lon_deg=135|lon_min=46|lon_sec=44.19|label=Kutsukawa
Kofun Cluster|position=top|width=220|Red pog.svg|marksize=10|caption={{center|Location of the Kutsukawa Kofun Cluster}}}} '''Kutsukawa Kofun Cluster''' (久津川古墳群) is a group of [[kofun]] burial mounds located in {{ill|Joyo|ja|城陽市}}, Kyoto Prefecture, Japan. Part of the cluster is designated as a National Historic Site and represents one of the largest kofun groups in Kyoto Prefecture.[http://mj-ktmr2.digi2.jp/p26ky/pys26207kutugawa.htm Kofun of Joyo City] == Overview == The Kutsukawa Kofun Cluster is situated in the lowlands and hills surrounding the Otanigawa River, east of {{ill|Kintetsu|ja|近畿日本鉄道}}'s Kutsukawa Station. Narrowly defined, the cluster includes around ten kofun near {{ill|Kutsukawa Kurazuka Kofun|ja|久津川車塚古墳}}, but when including smaller kofun scattered throughout the nearby hills, the total number of burial mounds is estimated to be around 150.[http://www.kyoto-kankou.or.jp/info_search/?id=379&r=1441389345.907 Kyoto Tourism Guide: Joyo City Kutsukawa Kofun Cluster] Many kofun have been lost or obscured due to recent residential development.[https://bunka.nii.ac.jp/heritages/detail/138764 Cultural Heritage Online: Kutsukawa Kurazuka and Marutsuka Kofun] Previously, {{ill|Kutsukawa Kurazuka Kofun|ja|久津川車塚古墳}} and {{ill|Maruzuka Kofun (Jōyō City)|ja|丸塚古墳 (城陽市)}} were designated collectively as the National Historic Site "Kutsukawa Kurazuka and Marutsuka Kofun." In 2016, {{ill|Basho-zuka Kofun|ja|芭蕉塚古墳}} and {{ill|Kuse Elementary School Kofun|ja|久世小学校古墳}} were added to the designation, and the name was changed to "Kutsukawa Kofun Cluster."{{PDFlink|[https://www.bunka.go.jp/koho_hodo_oshirase/hodohappyo/pdf/2016061701_besshi03.pdf Regarding Designations of Historic Sites]}} (Agency for Cultural Affairs, June 17, 2016).Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology Notification No. 144, October 3, 2016. Separately, Shibagahara No. 12 Kofun has been designated as the National Historic Site "{{ill|Shibagahara Kofun|ja|芝ヶ原古墳}}" and is not part of the "Kutsukawa Kofun Cluster." == Major Kofun == * **{{ill|Kutsukawa Kurazuka Kofun|ja|久津川車塚古墳}}** - National Historic Site. The largest keyhole-shaped kofun in the cluster and one of the largest in the Yamashiro region. A {{ill|Nagashigata stone coffin|ja|長持形石棺|1=Nagamochi style stone sarcophagus}} made of Ryuzan stone was discovered here. * **{{ill|Maruzuka Kofun (Jōyō City)|ja|丸塚古墳 (城陽市)}}** - National Historic Site. A scallop-shaped kofun. * **{{ill|Aotsuka Kofun|ja|青塚古墳 (城陽市)}}** - Rectangular front and rear burial mound. * **{{ill|Akatsuka Kofun|ja|赤塚古墳 (城陽市)}}** - Round burial mound adjacent to {{ill|Hirakawa Temple Ruins|ja|平川廃寺跡}}. * **{{ill|Basho-zuka Kofun|ja|芭蕉塚古墳}}** - National Historic Site. Keyhole-shaped kofun. * **Kajizuka Kofun** - Square burial mound partially overlapping Kutsukawa Kurazuka Kofun. * **Shigetsuzuka Kofun** - Round burial mound previously located on the grounds of {{ill|Joyo Municipal Kutsukawa Elementary School|ja|城陽市立久津川小学校}} but now lost due to construction. * **Hakozuka Kofun** - Keyhole-shaped kofun. * **Yamamichi Kofun** - Square burial mound lost due to residential development. * **{{ill|Shibagahara Kofun Group|ja|芝ヶ原古墳群}}** - A group of 13 kofun. Shibagahara No. 12 Kofun is designated as the National Historic Site "{{ill|Shibagahara Kofun|ja|芝ヶ原古墳}}," while Shibagahara No. 9 Kofun, located in the courtyard of {{ill|Joyo Municipal Kuse Elementary School|ja|城陽市立久世小学校}}, is designated as "{{ill|Kuse Elementary School Kofun|ja|久世小学校古墳}}." * **{{ill|Nitsuka Kofun Group|ja|尼塚古墳群}}** - A group of seven kofun. Nos. 1–5 have been lost, while Nos. 6 and 7 are preserved. * **Kami-Otani Kofun Group** - A group of 20 kofun, with 11 preserved. * **Shimo-Otani Kofun Group** - A group of two kofun. No. 2 has been lost, while No. 1 is preserved. * **{{ill|Nishiyama Kofun Group|ja|西山古墳群 (城陽市)}}** - Formerly near the Shimo-Otani group but lost due to residential development. * **Otakeshi Kofun** - Square burial mound. * **{{ill|Anjiyama Kofun|ja|庵寺山古墳}}** - Round burial mound. == Other Sites == * **{{ill|Hirakawa Temple Ruins|ja|平川廃寺跡}}** - National Historic Site adjacent to Akatsuka Kofun. * **{{ill|Kuse Temple Ruins|ja|久世廃寺跡}}** - National Historic Site. * **{{ill|Seido Administrative Complex Ruins|ja|正道官衙遺跡}}** - National Historic Site. == Cultural Properties == === Important Cultural Properties (National Designation) === * **Mirrors excavated from Kutsukawa Kurazuka Kofun (7 pieces, archaeological artifacts)** - Stored at {{ill|Sen-oku Hakukokan Museum|ja|泉屋博古館}}. Designated on November 14, 1953.{{National Cultural Property Database|201|9721|Mirrors Excavated from Kutsukawa Kurazuka Kofun}} * **Artifacts excavated from Shibagahara Kofun in Kyoto Prefecture (archaeological artifacts)** - Stored at Joyo City Historical Museum. Designated on June 29, 1990.{{National Cultural Property Database|201|10078|Artifacts Excavated from Shibagahara Kofun}} * **Nagashigata Stone Coffin excavated from Kutsukawa Kurazuka Kofun (archaeological artifacts)** - Stored at Kyoto University. Designated on June 21, 1991.{{National Cultural Property Database|201|10083|Nagashigata Stone Coffin Excavated from Kutsukawa Kurazuka Kofun}} === National Historic Sites === * **Kutsukawa Kofun Cluster** ** Kutsukawa Kurazuka Kofun ** Marutsuka Kofun ** Basho-zuka Kofun ** Kuse Elementary School Kofun *: Designated on January 19, 1979, as "Kutsukawa Kurazuka and Marutsuka Kofun." *: Renamed "Kutsukawa Kofun Cluster" with the inclusion of Basho-zuka and Kuse Elementary School Kofun on October 3, 2016.{{National Cultural Property Database|401|1741|Kutsukawa Kofun Cluster}} * **Shibagahara Kofun** *: Designated on September 6, 1989. *: Boundary expanded on January 24, 2012.{{National Cultural Property Database|401|1750|Shibagahara Kofun}} === Joyo City Designated Cultural Properties === * **Artifacts Excavated from Shibagahara No. 11 Kofun (archaeological artifacts)** File:芝ヶ原11号墳出土 三角縁銘帯三神四獣鏡.JPG|Triangular-rimmed mirror excavated from Shibagahara No. 11 Kofun

{{Location map|Japan Kyoto|lat_deg=34|lat_min=51|lat_sec=53.32|lon_deg=135|lon_min=46|lon_sec=44.19|label=Kutsukawa
Kofun Cluster|position=top|width=220|Red pog.svg|marksize=10|caption={{center|Location of the Kutsukawa Kofun Cluster}}}} '''Kutsukawa Kofun Cluster''' (久津川古墳群) is a group of [[kofun]] burial mounds located in {{ill|Joyo|ja|城陽市}}, Kyoto Prefecture, Japan. Part of the cluster is designated as a National Historic Site and represents one of the largest kofun groups in Kyoto Prefecture.[http://mj-ktmr2.digi2.jp/p26ky/pys26207kutugawa.htm Kofun of Joyo City] == Overview == The Kutsukawa Kofun Cluster is situated in the lowlands and hills surrounding the Otanigawa River, east of {{ill|Kintetsu|ja|近畿日本鉄道}}'s Kutsukawa Station. Narrowly defined, the cluster includes around ten kofun near {{ill|Kutsukawa Kurazuka Kofun|ja|久津川車塚古墳}}, but when including smaller kofun scattered throughout the nearby hills, the total number of burial mounds is estimated to be around 150.[http://www.kyoto-kankou.or.jp/info_search/?id=379&r=1441389345.907 Kyoto Tourism Guide: Joyo City Kutsukawa Kofun Cluster] Many kofun have been lost or obscured due to recent residential development.[https://bunka.nii.ac.jp/heritages/detail/138764 Cultural Heritage Online: Kutsukawa Kurazuka and Marutsuka Kofun] Previously, {{ill|Kutsukawa Kurazuka Kofun|ja|久津川車塚古墳}} and {{ill|Maruzuka Kofun (Jōyō City)|ja|丸塚古墳 (城陽市)}} were designated collectively as the National Historic Site "Kutsukawa Kurazuka and Marutsuka Kofun." In 2016, {{ill|Basho-zuka Kofun|ja|芭蕉塚古墳}} and {{ill|Kuse Elementary School Kofun|ja|久世小学校古墳}} were added to the designation, and the name was changed to "Kutsukawa Kofun Cluster."{{PDFlink|[https://www.bunka.go.jp/koho_hodo_oshirase/hodohappyo/pdf/2016061701_besshi03.pdf Regarding Designations of Historic Sites]}} (Agency for Cultural Affairs, June 17, 2016).Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology Notification No. 144, October 3, 2016. Separately, Shibagahara No. 12 Kofun has been designated as the National Historic Site "{{ill|Shibagahara Kofun|ja|芝ヶ原古墳}}" and is not part of the "Kutsukawa Kofun Cluster." == Major Kofun == * **{{ill|Kutsukawa Kurazuka Kofun|ja|久津川車塚古墳}}** - National Historic Site. The largest keyhole-shaped kofun in the cluster and one of the largest in the Yamashiro region. A {{ill|Nagashigata stone coffin|ja|長持形石棺|1=Nagamochi style stone sarcophagus}} made of Ryuzan stone was discovered here. * **{{ill|Maruzuka Kofun (Jōyō City)|ja|丸塚古墳 (城陽市)}}** - National Historic Site. A scallop-shaped kofun. * **{{ill|Aotsuka Kofun|ja|青塚古墳 (城陽市)}}** - Rectangular front and rear burial mound. * **{{ill|Akatsuka Kofun|ja|赤塚古墳 (城陽市)}}** - Round burial mound adjacent to {{ill|Hirakawa Temple Ruins|ja|平川廃寺跡}}. * **{{ill|Basho-zuka Kofun|ja|芭蕉塚古墳}}** - National Historic Site. Keyhole-shaped kofun. * **Kajizuka Kofun** - Square burial mound partially overlapping Kutsukawa Kurazuka Kofun. * **Shigetsuzuka Kofun** - Round burial mound previously located on the grounds of {{ill|Joyo Municipal Kutsukawa Elementary School|ja|城陽市立久津川小学校}} but now lost due to construction. * **Hakozuka Kofun** - Keyhole-shaped kofun. * **Yamamichi Kofun** - Square burial mound lost due to residential development. * **{{ill|Shibagahara Kofun Group|ja|芝ヶ原古墳群}}** - A group of 13 kofun. Shibagahara No. 12 Kofun is designated as the National Historic Site "{{ill|Shibagahara Kofun|ja|芝ヶ原古墳}}," while Shibagahara No. 9 Kofun, located in the courtyard of {{ill|Joyo Municipal Kuse Elementary School|ja|城陽市立久世小学校}}, is designated as "{{ill|Kuse Elementary School Kofun|ja|久世小学校古墳}}." * **{{ill|Nitsuka Kofun Group|ja|尼塚古墳群}}** - A group of seven kofun. Nos. 1–5 have been lost, while Nos. 6 and 7 are preserved. * **Kami-Otani Kofun Group** - A group of 20 kofun, with 11 preserved. * **Shimo-Otani Kofun Group** - A group of two kofun. No. 2 has been lost, while No. 1 is preserved. * **{{ill|Nishiyama Kofun Group|ja|西山古墳群 (城陽市)}}** - Formerly near the Shimo-Otani group but lost due to residential development. * **Otakeshi Kofun** - Square burial mound. * **{{ill|Anjiyama Kofun|ja|庵寺山古墳}}** - Round burial mound. == Other Sites == * **{{ill|Hirakawa Temple Ruins|ja|平川廃寺跡}}** - National Historic Site adjacent to Akatsuka Kofun. * **{{ill|Kuse Temple Ruins|ja|久世廃寺跡}}** - National Historic Site. * **{{ill|Seido Administrative Complex Ruins|ja|正道官衙遺跡}}** - National Historic Site. == Cultural Properties == === Important Cultural Properties (National Designation) === * **Mirrors excavated from Kutsukawa Kurazuka Kofun (7 pieces, archaeological artifacts)** - Stored at {{ill|Sen-oku Hakukokan Museum|ja|泉屋博古館}}. Designated on November 14, 1953.{{National Cultural Property Database|201|9721|Mirrors Excavated from Kutsukawa Kurazuka Kofun}} * **Artifacts excavated from Shibagahara Kofun in Kyoto Prefecture (archaeological artifacts)** - Stored at Joyo City Historical Museum. Designated on June 29, 1990.{{National Cultural Property Database|201|10078|Artifacts Excavated from Shibagahara Kofun}} * **Nagashigata Stone Coffin excavated from Kutsukawa Kurazuka Kofun (archaeological artifacts)** - Stored at Kyoto University. {{Location map|Japan Kyoto|lat_deg=34|lat_min=51|lat_sec=53.32|lon_deg=135|lon_min=46|lon_sec=44.19|label=Kutsukawa
Kofun Cluster|position=top|width=220|Red pog.svg|marksize=10|caption={{center|Location of the Kutsukawa Kofun Cluster}}}} '''Kutsukawa Kofun Cluster''' (久津川古墳群) is a group of [[kofun]] burial mounds located in {{ill|Joyo|ja|城陽市}}, Kyoto Prefecture, Japan. Part of the cluster is designated as a National Historic Site and represents one of the largest kofun groups in Kyoto Prefecture.[http://mj-ktmr2.digi2.jp/p26ky/pys26207kutugawa.htm Kofun of Joyo City] == Overview == The Kutsukawa Kofun Cluster is situated in the lowlands and hills surrounding the Otanigawa River, east of {{ill|Kintetsu|ja|近畿日本鉄道}}'s Kutsukawa Station. Narrowly defined, the cluster includes around ten kofun near {{ill|Kutsukawa Kurazuka Kofun|ja|久津川車塚古墳}}, but when including smaller kofun scattered throughout the nearby hills, the total number of burial mounds is estimated to be around 150.[http://www.kyoto-kankou.or.jp/info_search/?id=379&r=1441389345.907 Kyoto Tourism Guide: Joyo City Kutsukawa Kofun Cluster] Many kofun have been lost or obscured due to recent residential development.[https://bunka.nii.ac.jp/heritages/detail/138764 Cultural Heritage Online: Kutsukawa Kurazuka and Marutsuka Kofun] Previously, {{ill|Kutsukawa Kurazuka Kofun|ja|久津川車塚古墳}} and {{ill|Maruzuka Kofun (Jōyō City)|ja|丸塚古墳 (城陽市)}} were designated collectively as the National Historic Site "Kutsukawa Kurazuka and Marutsuka Kofun." In 2016, {{ill|Basho-zuka Kofun|ja|芭蕉塚古墳}} and {{ill|Kuse Elementary School Kofun|ja|久世小学校古墳}} were added to the designation, and the name was changed to "Kutsukawa Kofun Cluster."{{PDFlink|[https://www.bunka.go.jp/koho_hodo_oshirase/hodohappyo/pdf/2016061701_besshi03.pdf Regarding Designations of Historic Sites]}} (Agency for Cultural Affairs, June 17, 2016).Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology Notification No. 144, October 3, 2016. Separately, Shibagahara No. 12 Kofun has been designated as the National Historic Site "{{ill|Shibagahara Kofun|ja|芝ヶ原古墳}}" and is not part of the "Kutsukawa Kofun Cluster." == Major Kofun == * **{{ill|Kutsukawa Kurazuka Kofun|ja|久津川車塚古墳}}** - National Historic Site. The largest keyhole-shaped kofun in the cluster and one of the largest in the Yamashiro region. A {{ill|Nagashigata stone coffin|ja|長持形石棺|1=Nagamochi style stone sarcophagus}} made of Ryuzan stone was discovered here. * **{{ill|Maruzuka Kofun (Jōyō City)|ja|丸塚古墳 (城陽市)}}** - National Historic Site. A scallop-shaped kofun. * **{{ill|Aotsuka Kofun|ja|青塚古墳 (城陽市)}}** - Rectangular front and rear burial mound. * **{{ill|Akatsuka Kofun|ja|赤塚古墳 (城陽市)}}** - Round burial mound adjacent to {{ill|Hirakawa Temple Ruins|ja|平川廃寺跡}}. * **{{ill|Basho-zuka Kofun|ja|芭蕉塚古墳}}** - National Historic Site. Keyhole-shaped kofun. * **Kajizuka Kofun** - Square burial mound partially overlapping Kutsukawa Kurazuka Kofun. * **Shigetsuzuka Kofun** - Round burial mound previously located on the grounds of {{ill|Joyo Municipal Kutsukawa Elementary School|ja|城陽市立久津川小学校}} but now lost due to construction. * **Hakozuka Kofun** - Keyhole-shaped kofun. * **Yamamichi Kofun** - Square burial mound lost due to residential development. * **{{ill|Shibagahara Kofun Group|ja|芝ヶ原古墳群}}** - A group of 13 kofun. Shibagahara No. 12 Kofun is designated as the National Historic Site "{{ill|Shibagahara Kofun|ja|芝ヶ原古墳}}," while Shibagahara No. 9 Kofun, located in the courtyard of {{ill|Joyo Municipal Kuse Elementary School|ja|城陽市立久世小学校}}, is designated as "{{ill|Kuse Elementary School Kofun|ja|久世小学校古墳}}." * **{{ill|Nitsuka Kofun Group|ja|尼塚古墳群}}** - A group of seven kofun. Nos. 1–5 have been lost, while Nos. 6 and 7 are preserved. * **Kami-Otani Kofun Group** - A group of 20 kofun, with 11 preserved. * **Shimo-Otani Kofun Group** - A group of two kofun. No. 2 has been lost, while No. 1 is preserved. * **{{ill|Nishiyama Kofun Group|ja|西山古墳群 (城陽市)}}** - Formerly near the Shimo-Otani group but lost due to residential development. * **Otakeshi Kofun** - Square burial mound. * **{{ill|Anjiyama Kofun|ja|庵寺山古墳}}** - Round burial mound. == Other Sites == * **{{ill|Hirakawa Temple Ruins|ja|平川廃寺跡}}** - National Historic Site adjacent to Akatsuka Kofun. * **{{ill|Kuse Temple Ruins|ja|久世廃寺跡}}** - National Historic Site. * **{{ill|Seido Administrative Complex Ruins|ja|正道官衙遺跡}}** - National Historic Site. == Cultural Properties == === Important Cultural Properties (National Designation) === * **Mirrors excavated from Kutsukawa Kurazuka Kofun (7 pieces, archaeological artifacts)** - Stored at {{ill|Sen-oku Hakukokan Museum|ja|泉屋博古館}}. Designated on November 14, 1953.{{National Cultural Property Database|201|9721|Mirrors Excavated from Kutsukawa Kurazuka Kofun}} * **Artifacts excavated from Shibagahara Kofun in Kyoto Prefecture (archaeological artifacts)** - Stored at Joyo City Historical Museum. Designated on June 29, 1990.{{National Cultural Property Database|201|10078|Artifacts Excavated from Shibagahara Kofun}} * **Nagashigata Stone Coffin excavated from Kutsukawa Kurazuka Kofun (archaeological artifacts)** - Stored at Kyoto University. Designated on June 21, 1991.{{National Cultural Property Database|201|10083|Nagashigata Stone Coffin Excavated from Kutsukawa Kurazuka Kofun}} === National Historic Sites === * **Kutsukawa Kofun Cluster** ** Kutsukawa Kurazuka Kofun ** Marutsuka Kofun ** Basho-zuka Kofun ** Kuse Elementary School Kofun *: Designated on January 19, 1979, as "Kutsukawa Kurazuka and Marutsuka Kofun." *: Renamed "Kutsukawa Kofun Cluster" with the inclusion of Basho-zuka and Kuse Elementary School Kofun on October 3, 2016.{{National Cultural Property Database|401|1741|Kutsukawa Kofun Cluster}} * **Shibagahara Kofun** *: Designated on September 6, 1989. *: Boundary expanded on January 24, 2012.{{National Cultural Property Database|401|1750|Shibagahara Kofun}} === Joyo City Designated Cultural Properties === * **Artifacts Excavated from Shibagahara No. 11 Kofun (archaeological artifacts)** File:芝ヶ原11号墳出土 三角縁銘帯三神四獣鏡.JPG|Triangular-rimmed mirror excavated from Shibagahara No. 11 Kofun
{{small|Exhibited at the Joyo City Historical Museum (Gorikan).}} == Access == * Approximately 10–45 minutes on foot from {{ill|Kintetsu|ja|近畿日本鉄道}} Kutsukawa Station. * Approximately 10–45 minutes on foot from {{ill|JR West Nara Line|ja|奈良線}} Joyo Station. == References == {{Reflist}} == Sources == * [http://www.city.joyo.kyoto.jp/introduction/asset/kuni-siseki/kuni-siseki2 Official Page on {{Location map|Japan Kyoto|lat_deg=34|lat_min=51|lat_sec=53.32|lon_deg=135|lon_min=46|lon_sec=44.19|label=Kutsukawa
Kofun Cluster|position=top|width=220|Red pog.svg|marksize=10|caption={{center|Location of the Kutsukawa Kofun Cluster}}}} '''Kutsukawa Kofun Cluster''' (久津川古墳群) is a group of [[kofun]] burial mounds located in {{ill|Joyo|ja|城陽市}}, Kyoto Prefecture, Japan. Part of the cluster is designated as a National Historic Site and represents one of the largest kofun groups in Kyoto Prefecture.[http://mj-ktmr2.digi2.jp/p26ky/pys26207kutugawa.htm Kofun of Joyo City] == Overview == The Kutsukawa Kofun Cluster is situated in the lowlands and hills surrounding the Otanigawa River, east of {{ill|Kintetsu|ja|近畿日本鉄道}}'s Kutsukawa Station. Narrowly defined, the cluster includes around ten kofun near {{ill|Kutsukawa Kurazuka Kofun|ja|久津川車塚古墳}}, but when including smaller kofun scattered throughout the nearby hills, the total number of burial mounds is estimated to be around 150.[http://www.kyoto-kankou.or.jp/info_search/?id=379&r=1441389345.907 Kyoto Tourism Guide: Joyo City Kutsukawa Kofun Cluster] Many kofun have been lost or obscured due to recent residential development.[https://bunka.nii.ac.jp/heritages/detail/138764 Cultural Heritage Online: Kutsukawa Kurazuka and Marutsuka Kofun] Previously, {{ill|Kutsukawa Kurazuka Kofun|ja|久津川車塚古墳}} and {{ill|Maruzuka Kofun (Jōyō City)|ja|丸塚古墳 (城陽市)}} were designated collectively as the National Historic Site "Kutsukawa Kurazuka and Marutsuka Kofun." In 2016, {{ill|Basho-zuka Kofun|ja|芭蕉塚古墳}} and {{ill|Kuse Elementary School Kofun|ja|久世小学校古墳}} were added to the designation, and the name was changed to "Kutsukawa Kofun Cluster."{{PDFlink|[https://www.bunka.go.jp/koho_hodo_oshirase/hodohappyo/pdf/2016061701_besshi03.pdf Regarding Designations of Historic Sites]}} (Agency for Cultural Affairs, June 17, 2016).Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology Notification No. 144, October 3, 2016. Separately, Shibagahara No. 12 Kofun has been designated as the National Historic Site "{{ill|Shibagahara Kofun|ja|芝ヶ原古墳}}" and is not part of the "Kutsukawa Kofun Cluster." == Major Kofun == * **{{ill|Kutsukawa Kurazuka Kofun|ja|久津川車塚古墳}}** - National Historic Site. Keyhole-shaped kofun. * **Kajizuka Kofun** - Square burial mound partially overlapping Kutsukawa Kurazuka Kofun. * **Shigetsuzuka Kofun** - Round burial mound previously located on the grounds of {{ill|Joyo Municipal Kutsukawa Elementary School|ja|城陽市立久津川小学校}} but now lost due to construction. * **Hakozuka Kofun** - Keyhole-shaped kofun. * **Yamamichi Kofun** - Square burial mound lost due to residential development. * **{{ill|Shibagahara Kofun Group|ja|芝ヶ原古墳群}}** - A group of 13 kofun. Shibagahara No. 12 Kofun is designated as the National Historic Site "{{ill|Shibagahara Kofun|ja|芝ヶ原古墳}}," while Shibagahara No. 9 Kofun, located in the courtyard of {{ill|Joyo Municipal Kuse Elementary School|ja|城陽市立久世小学校}}, is designated as "{{ill|Kuse Elementary School Kofun|ja|久世小学校古墳}}." * **{{ill|Nitsuka Kofun Group|ja|尼塚古墳群}}** - A group of seven kofun. Nos. 1–5 have been lost, while Nos. 6 and 7 are preserved. * **Kami-Otani Kofun Group** - A group of 20 kofun, with 11 preserved. * **Shimo-Otani Kofun Group** - A group of two kofun. No. 2 has been lost, while No. 1 is preserved. * **{{ill|Nishiyama Kofun Group|ja|西山古墳群 (城陽市)}}** - Formerly near the Shimo-Otani group but lost due to residential development. * **Otakeshi Kofun** - Square burial mound. * **{{ill|Anjiyama Kofun|ja|庵寺山古墳}}** - Round burial mound. == Other Sites == * **{{ill|Hirakawa Temple Ruins|ja|平川廃寺跡}}** - National Historic Site adjacent to Akatsuka Kofun. * **{{ill|Kuse Temple Ruins|ja|久世廃寺跡}}** - National Historic Site. * **{{ill|Seido Administrative Complex Ruins|ja|正道官衙遺跡}}** - National Historic Site. == Cultural Properties == === Important Cultural Properties (National Designation) === * **Mirrors excavated from Kutsukawa Kurazuka Kofun (7 pieces, archaeological artifacts)** - Stored at {{ill|Sen-oku Hakukokan Museum|ja|泉屋博古館}}. {{Location map|Japan Kyoto|lat_deg=34|lat_min=51|lat_sec=53.32|lon_deg=135|lon_min=46|lon_sec=44.19|label=Kutsukawa
Kofun Cluster|position=top|width=220|Red pog.svg|marksize=10|caption={{center|Location of the Kutsukawa Kofun Cluster}}}} '''Kutsukawa Kofun Cluster''' (久津川古墳群) is a group of [[kofun]] burial mounds located in {{ill|Joyo|ja|城陽市}}, Kyoto Prefecture, Japan. Part of the cluster is designated as a National Historic Site and represents one of the largest kofun groups in Kyoto Prefecture.[http://mj-ktmr2.digi2.jp/p26ky/pys26207kutugawa.htm Kofun of Joyo City] == Overview == The Kutsukawa Kofun Cluster is situated in the lowlands and hills surrounding the Otanigawa River, east of {{ill|Kintetsu|ja|近畿日本鉄道}}'s Kutsukawa Station. Narrowly defined, the cluster includes around ten kofun near {{ill|Kutsukawa Kurazuka Kofun|ja|久津川車塚古墳}}, but when including smaller kofun scattered throughout the nearby hills, the total number of burial mounds is estimated to be around 150.[http://www.kyoto-kankou.or.jp/info_search/?id=379&r=1441389345.907 Kyoto Tourism Guide: Joyo City Kutsukawa Kofun Cluster] Many kofun have been lost or obscured due to recent residential development.[https://bunka.nii.ac.jp/heritages/detail/138764 Cultural Heritage Online: Kutsukawa Kurazuka and Marutsuka Kofun] Previously, {{ill|Kutsukawa Kurazuka Kofun|ja|久津川車塚古墳}} and {{ill|Maruzuka Kofun (Jōyō City)|ja|丸塚古墳 (城陽市)}} were designated collectively as the National Historic Site "Kutsukawa Kurazuka and Marutsuka Kofun." In 2016, {{ill|Basho-zuka Kofun|ja|芭蕉塚古墳}} and {{ill|Kuse Elementary School Kofun|ja|久世小学校古墳}} were added to the designation, and the name was changed to "Kutsukawa Kofun Cluster."{{PDFlink|[https://www.bunka.go.jp/koho_hodo_oshirase/hodohappyo/pdf/2016061701_besshi03.pdf Regarding Designations of Historic Sites]}} (Agency for Cultural Affairs, June 17, 2016).Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology Notification No. 144, October 3, 2016. Separately, Shibagahara No. 12 Kofun has been designated as the National Historic Site "{{ill|Shibagahara Kofun|ja|芝ヶ原古墳}}" and is not part of the "Kutsukawa Kofun Cluster." == Major Kofun == * **{{ill|Kutsukawa Kurazuka Kofun|ja|久津川車塚古墳}}** - National Historic Site. The largest keyhole-shaped kofun in the cluster and one of the largest in the Yamashiro region. A {{ill|Nagashigata stone coffin|ja|長持形石棺|1=Nagamochi style stone sarcophagus}} made of Ryuzan stone was discovered here. * **{{ill|Maruzuka Kofun (Jōyō City)|ja|丸塚古墳 (城陽市)}}** - National Historic Site. A scallop-shaped kofun. * **{{ill|Aotsuka Kofun|ja|青塚古墳 (城陽市)}}** - Rectangular front and rear burial mound. * **{{ill|Akatsuka Kofun|ja|赤塚古墳 (城陽市)}}** - Round burial mound adjacent to {{ill|Hirakawa Temple Ruins|ja|平川廃寺跡}}. * **{{ill|Basho-zuka Kofun|ja|芭蕉塚古墳}}** - National Historic Site. Keyhole-shaped kofun. * **Kajizuka Kofun** - Square burial mound partially overlapping Kutsukawa Kurazuka Kofun. * **Shigetsuzuka Kofun** - Round burial mound previously located on the grounds of {{ill|Joyo Municipal Kutsukawa Elementary School|ja|城陽市立久津川小学校}} but now lost due to construction. * **Hakozuka Kofun** - Keyhole-shaped kofun. * **Yamamichi Kofun** - Square burial mound lost due to residential development. * **{{ill|Shibagahara Kofun Group|ja|芝ヶ原古墳群}}** - A group of 13 kofun. Shibagahara No. 12 Kofun is designated as the National Historic Site "{{ill|Shibagahara Kofun|ja|芝ヶ原古墳}}," while Shibagahara No. 9 Kofun, located in the courtyard of {{ill|Joyo Municipal Kuse Elementary School|ja|城陽市立久世小学校}}, is designated as "{{ill|Kuse Elementary School Kofun|ja|久世小学校古墳}}." * **{{ill|Nitsuka Kofun Group|ja|尼塚古墳群}}** - A group of seven kofun. Nos. 1–5 have been lost, while Nos. 6 and 7 are preserved. * **Kami-Otani Kofun Group** - A group of 20 kofun, with 11 preserved. * **Shimo-Otani Kofun Group** - A group of two kofun. No. 2 has been lost, while No. 1 is preserved. * **{{ill|Nishiyama Kofun Group|ja|西山古墳群 (城陽市)}}** - Formerly near the Shimo-Otani group but lost due to residential development. * **Otakeshi Kofun** - Square burial mound. * **{{ill|Anjiyama Kofun|ja|庵寺山古墳}}** - Round burial mound. == Other Sites == * **{{ill|Hirakawa Temple Ruins|ja|平川廃寺跡}}** - National Historic Site adjacent to Akatsuka Kofun. * **{{ill|Kuse Temple Ruins|ja|久世廃寺跡}}** - National Historic Site. * **{{ill|Seido Administrative Complex Ruins|ja|正道官衙遺跡}}** - National Historic Site. == Cultural Properties == === Important Cultural Properties (National Designation) === * **Mirrors excavated from Kutsukawa Kurazuka Kofun (7 pieces, archaeological artifacts)** - Stored at {{ill|Sen-oku Hakukokan Museum|ja|泉屋博古館}}. Designated on November 14, 1953.{{National Cultural Property Database|201|9721|Mirrors Excavated from Kutsukawa Kurazuka Kofun}} * **Artifacts excavated from Shibagahara Kofun in Kyoto Prefecture (archaeological artifacts)** - Stored at Joyo City Historical Museum. Designated on June 29, 1990.{{National Cultural Property Database|201|10078|Artifacts Excavated from Shibagahara Kofun}} * **Nagashigata Stone Coffin excavated from Kutsukawa Kurazuka Kofun (archaeological artifacts)** - Stored at Kyoto University. Designated on June 21, 1991.{{National Cultural Property Database|201|10083|Nagashigata Stone Coffin Excavated from Kutsukawa Kurazuka Kofun}} === National Historic Sites === * **Kutsukawa Kofun Cluster** ** Kutsukawa Kurazuka Kofun ** Marutsuka Kofun ** Basho-zuka Kofun ** Kuse Elementary School Kofun *: Designated on January 19, 1979, as "Kutsukawa Kurazuka and Marutsuka Kofun." *: Renamed "Kutsukawa Kofun Cluster" with the inclusion of Basho-zuka and Kuse Elementary School Kofun on October 3, 2016.{{National Cultural Property Database|401|1741|Kutsukawa Kofun Cluster}} * **Shibagahara Kofun** *: Designated on September 6, 1989. *: Boundary expanded on January 24, 2012.{{National Cultural Property Database|401|1750|Shibagahara Kofun}} === Joyo City Designated Cultural Properties === * **Artifacts Excavated from Shibagahara No. 11 Kofun (archaeological artifacts)** File:芝ヶ原11号墳出土 三角縁銘帯三神四獣鏡.JPG|Triangular-rimmed mirror excavated from Shibagahara No. 11 Kofun
{{small|Exhibited at the Joyo City Historical Museum (Gorikan).}} == Access == * Approximately 10–45 minutes on foot from {{ill|Kintetsu|ja|近畿日本鉄道}} Kutsukawa Station. * Approximately 10–45 minutes on foot from {{ill|JR West Nara Line|ja|奈良線}} Joyo Station. == References == {{Reflist}} == Sources == * [http://www.city.joyo.kyoto.jp/introduction/asset/kuni-siseki/kuni-siseki2 Official Page on Kutsukawa Kurazuka and Marutsuka Kofun] * [http://obito1.web.fc2.com/zyouyou.html Ancient Burial Mounds of Joyo City] * [https://bunka.nii.ac.jp/heritages/detail/138764 Cultural Heritage Online: Kutsukawa Kurazuka and Marutsuka Kofun] * [http://www.kyoto-kankou.or.jp/info_search/?id=379&r=1441389345.907 Kyoto Tourism Guide: Kutsukawa Kofun Cluster] * [http://mj-ktmr2.digi2.jp/p26ky/pys26207kutugawa.htm Kofun of Joyo City] * [http://www.jpn-hayashi.com/cgi-bin/pjlist.cgi?mode=%8Es%93%E0&title0=%8F%E9%97z%8Es&title2=%82%C9%82%A0%82%E9%8C%C3%95%AD&choice1=%8Es%93%E0&area0=%8Es%93%E0&area1=%8B%9E%93s%95%7B&area2=&area3=%8F%E9%97z%8Es&item0=1&item2=54&item3=100&browser=99&colum=24&font=20&screen=240&life= {{Location map|Japan Kyoto|lat_deg=34|lat_min=51|lat_sec=53.32|lon_deg=135|lon_min=46|lon_sec=44.19|label=Kutsukawa
Kofun Cluster|position=top|width=220|Red pog.svg|marksize=10|caption={{center|Location of the Kutsukawa Kofun Cluster}}}} '''Kutsukawa Kofun Cluster''' (久津川古墳群) is a group of [[kofun]] Kofuns located in {{ill|Joyo|ja|城陽市}}, Kyoto Prefecture, Japan. Part of the cluster is designated as a National Historic Site and represents one of the largest kofun groups in Kyoto Prefecture.[http://mj-ktmr2.digi2.jp/p26ky/pys26207kutugawa.htm Kofun of Joyo City] == Overview == The Kutsukawa Kofun Cluster is situated in the lowlands and hills surrounding the Otanigawa River, east of {{ill|Kintetsu|ja|近畿日本鉄道}}'s Kutsukawa Station. Narrowly defined, the cluster includes around ten kofun near {{ill|Kutsukawa Kurazuka Kofun|ja|久津川車塚古墳}}, but when including smaller kofun scattered throughout the nearby hills, the total number of Kofuns is estimated to be around 150.[http://www.kyoto-kankou.or.jp/info_search/?id=379&r=1441389345.907 Kyoto Tourism Guide: Joyo City Kutsukawa Kofun Cluster] Many kofun have been lost or obscured due to recent residential development.[https://bunka.nii.ac.jp/heritages/detail/138764 Cultural Heritage Online: Kutsukawa Kurazuka and Marutsuka Kofun] Previously, {{ill|Kutsukawa Kurazuka Kofun|ja|久津川車塚古墳}} and {{ill|Maruzuka Kofun (Jōyō City)|ja|丸塚古墳 (城陽市)}} were designated collectively as the National Historic Site "Kutsukawa Kurazuka and Marutsuka Kofun." In 2016, {{ill|Basho-zuka Kofun|ja|芭蕉塚古墳}} and {{ill|Kuse Elementary School Kofun|ja|久世小学校古墳}} were added to the designation, and the name was changed to "Kutsukawa Kofun Cluster."{{PDFlink|[https://www.bunka.go.jp/koho_hodo_oshirase/hodohappyo/pdf/2016061701_besshi03.pdf Regarding Designations of Historic Sites]}} (Agency for Cultural Affairs, June 17, 2016).Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology Notification No. 144, October 3, 2016. Separately, Shibagahara No. 12 Kofun has been designated as the National Historic Site "{{ill|Shibagahara Kofun|ja|芝ヶ原古墳}}" and is not part of the "Kutsukawa Kofun Cluster." == Major Kofun == * **{{ill|Kutsukawa Kurazuka Kofun|ja|久津川車塚古墳}}** - National Historic Site. The largest keyhole-shaped kofun in the cluster and one of the largest in the Yamashiro region. A {{ill|Nagashigata stone coffin|ja|長持形石棺|1=Nagamochi style stone sarcophagus}} made of Ryuzan stone was discovered here. * **{{ill|Maruzuka Kofun (Jōyō City)|ja|丸塚古墳 (城陽市)}}** - National Historic Site. A scallop-shaped kofun. * **{{ill|Aotsuka Kofun|ja|青塚古墳 (城陽市)}}** - Rectangular front and rear Kofun. * **{{ill|Akatsuka Kofun|ja|赤塚古墳 (城陽市)}}** - Round Kofun adjacent to {{ill|Hirakawa Temple Ruins|ja|平川廃寺跡}}. * **{{ill|Basho-zuka Kofun|ja|芭蕉塚古墳}}** - National Historic Site. Keyhole-shaped kofun. * **Kajizuka Kofun** - Square Kofun partially overlapping Kutsukawa Kurazuka Kofun. * **Shigetsuzuka Kofun** - Round Kofun previously located on the grounds of {{ill|Joyo Municipal Kutsukawa Elementary School|ja|城陽市立久津川小学校}} but now lost due to construction. * **Hakozuka Kofun** - Keyhole-shaped kofun. * **Yamamichi Kofun** - Square Kofun lost due to residential development. * **{{ill|Shibagahara Kofun Group|ja|芝ヶ原古墳群}}** - A group of 13 kofun. Shibagahara No. 12 Kofun is designated as the National Historic Site "{{ill|Shibagahara Kofun|ja|芝ヶ原古墳}}," while Shibagahara No. 9 Kofun, located in the courtyard of {{ill|Joyo Municipal Kuse Elementary School|ja|城陽市立久世小学校}}, is designated as "{{ill|Kuse Elementary School Kofun|ja|久世小学校古墳}}." * **{{ill|Nitsuka Kofun Group|ja|尼塚古墳群}}** - A group of seven kofun. Nos. 1–5 have been lost, while Nos. 6 and 7 are preserved. * **Kami-Otani Kofun Group** - A group of 20 kofun, with 11 preserved. * **Shimo-Otani Kofun Group** - A group of two kofun. No. 2 has been lost, while No. 1 is preserved. * **{{ill|Nishiyama Kofun Group|ja|西山古墳群 (城陽市)}}** - Formerly near the Shimo-Otani group but lost due to residential development. * **Otakeshi Kofun** - Square Kofun. * **{{ill|Anjiyama Kofun|ja|庵寺山古墳}}** - Round Kofun. == Other Sites == * **{{ill|Hirakawa Temple Ruins|ja|平川廃寺跡}}** - National Historic Site adjacent to Akatsuka Kofun. * **{{ill|Kuse Temple Ruins|ja|久世廃寺跡}}** - National Historic Site. * **{{ill|Seido Administrative Complex Ruins|ja|正道官衙遺跡}}** - National Historic Site. == Cultural Properties == === Important Cultural Properties (National Designation) === * **Mirrors excavated from Kutsukawa Kurazuka Kofun (7 pieces, archaeological artifacts)** - Stored at {{ill|Sen-oku Hakukokan Museum|ja|泉屋博古館}}. Designated on November 14, 1953.{{National Cultural Property Database|201|9721|Mirrors Excavated from Kutsukawa Kurazuka Kofun}} * **Artifacts excavated from Shibagahara Kofun in Kyoto Prefecture (archaeological artifacts)** - Stored at Joyo City Historical Museum. Designated on June 29, 1990.{{National Cultural Property Database|201|10078|Artifacts Excavated from Shibagahara Kofun}} * **Nagashigata Stone Coffin excavated from Kutsukawa Kurazuka Kofun (archaeological artifacts)** - Stored at Kyoto University. Designated on June 21, 1991.{{National Cultural Property Database|201|10083|Nagashigata Stone Coffin Excavated from Kutsukawa Kurazuka Kofun}} === National Historic Sites === * **Kutsukawa Kofun Cluster** ** Kutsukawa Kurazuka Kofun ** Marutsuka Kofun ** Basho-zuka Kofun ** Kuse Elementary School Kofun *: Designated on January 19, 1979, as "Kutsukawa Kurazuka and Marutsuka Kofun." *: Renamed "Kutsukawa Kofun Cluster" with the inclusion of Basho-zuka and Kuse Elementary School Kofun on October 3, 2016.{{National Cultural Property Database|401|1741|Kutsukawa Kofun Cluster}} * **Shibagahara Kofun** *: Designated on September 6, 1989. *: Boundary expanded on January 24, 2012.{{National Cultural Property Database|401|1750|Shibagahara Kofun}} === Joyo City Designated Cultural Properties === * **Artifacts Excavated from Shibagahara No. 11 Kofun (archaeological artifacts)** File:芝ヶ原11号墳出土 三角縁銘帯三神四獣鏡.JPG|Triangular-rimmed mirror excavated from Shibagahara No. 11 Kofun
